## BATCH 3 — DECISIVE: `view_renderer.cpp` and `real_layout.cpp` are **NOT COMPILED**. Most of my §C–§L findings were against dead code.

This batch supersedes the framing of batches 1–2. It is proven three independent ways.

### Proof 1 — the build manifest
`miniandroid/core_sources.manifest` lists **87 active translation units**. `CMakeLists.txt:93-105`:
```cmake
# GP583-BUILD-002 fix: the source list now comes from the SAME manifest the
# Makefile consumes (miniandroid/core_sources.manifest; 87 active TUs …)
file(STRINGS "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/core_sources.manifest" MINIANDROID_CORE_SOURCES …)
add_library(miniandroid_core STATIC ${MINIANDROID_CORE_SOURCES})
```
Neither `src/renderer/view_renderer.cpp` nor `src/resources/real_layout.cpp` appears in it.

### Proof 2 — CMakeLists has no reference at all
`grep view_renderer CMakeLists.txt` → **0 hits**. `grep real_layout CMakeLists.txt` → **0 hits**.
(For contrast, `dalvik_engine.cpp` *is* explicitly added at `:184` despite being absent from the manifest — so "absent from manifest" alone is not proof; the zero CMake reference is.)

### Proof 3 — the engine says so in a comment
`runtime/execution_engine.cpp:9222-9223`:
```cpp
// mirrors ViewRenderer::hit_test semantics without instantiating the
// (currently unlinked) renderer.
```

### The authoritative layout path (verified)
```cpp
// runtime/execution_engine.cpp:3816
if (rt.loaded() || vs_dirty || inflated_attach_consumed) {
    … F-NEW-403 LayoutParams live-state refresh …
    … F712 overrides_on_measure sync …
    // :3956
    rt.inflater().measure_layout(view_shadow, root_id);
    frame_census_.measure_ran  = true;
    frame_census_.layout_ran   = true;
    frame_census_.layout_source = "inflater";      // :3961
    if (view_shadow != nullptr) view_shadow->layout_dirty = false;   // :3966
}
```
**`layout_inflater.cpp::measure_layout` is the real engine.** `frame_census_.layout_source` is a built-in provenance field — use it in every future layout report.

### The #606 gate hypothesis is ALREADY FIXED
`execution_engine.cpp:3779-3789`:
```cpp
// R-NEW-302 FIX (AOSP requestLayout law): also re-measure when the DEX app
// mutated the view tree since the last frame (addView/removeView/
// setLayoutParams raise ViewShadow::layout_dirty).
// The old rt.loaded()-only gate meant programmatic trees (no resources.arsc)
// measured ONCE at setContentView and every later frame reused that stale
// geometry — the demo stage box was pinned at its first position forever.
const bool vs_dirty = view_shadow != nullptr && view_shadow->layout_dirty;
```
Plus `ADDITIONAL-AUDIT P0-1` attach-before-measure at `:3790-3814`. **Do not re-file the #606 gate as an open bug.** The remaining open question is narrower: what happens on a frame where all three conditions are false — is stale geometry reused, and is that correct?

## NEW-8 (P1, `[V]`) — a single 5.15 MB translation unit
`CMakeLists.txt:179-184`:
```cmake
# dalvik_engine.cpp (~5.0 MiB) and android_shadows.cpp (~646 KiB) blow the …
${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/dex/dalvik_engine.cpp
```
A 5 MiB TU cannot be incrementally compiled, cannot be parallelised, dominates peak compiler RSS, and is the reason a constrained CI worker OOMs. Combined with `android_shadows.cpp` (649 KB / 12,122 lines) this is the build-time bottleneck.
**Fix:** split by domain the way `dalvik_bridge_domain_*.cpp` already is (that pattern exists and works — 7 domain files). Target ≤ 2,000 lines/TU. This directly enables the sandbox/CI builds that are currently blocked.
`[R]` Unity/split-TU tradeoffs and compiler memory: https://cmake.org/cmake/help/latest/prop_tgt/UNITY_BUILD.html · https://gcc.gnu.org/wiki/SpeedupAreas

`CMakeLists.txt:415` and `CMakeLists.txt:435` both declare the target `miniandroid_test`.
```cmake
if(EXISTS ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/exp003a_main.cpp)  # BUILD-TRAIN: dead-target guard (cleanup waves removed sources; cmake-4.x …)
```
Silently skipping a target when its source vanished means **a cleanup wave can delete a test and the build stays green**. That is a false-green channel. Prefer an explicit `option(MINIANDROID_BUILD_EXP003A …)` plus a hard error when the option is ON and the source is missing.

## BATCH 5 — Text pipeline audit: professional stack, but a **P0 Persian/Arabic shaping-order defect** and no font fallback chain

`fonts/text_shaper.cpp` (manifest TU, 1,539 lines) is a real **FriBidi → HarfBuzz → FreeType** pipeline (`:3`). That retracts most of §N. But two genuine defects remain, and one of them is the highest-severity live finding in this registry so far for a Persian-language corpus.

### Retractions from §N
| ID | Verdict |
|---|---|
| N1 (measure vs draw metrics) | `[F]` largely wrong — `:840-841` "G36 law (was: size*1.2 ad-hoc): Android `Paint.getFontMetricsInt(null)` returns `descent - ascent` (`TextView.getLineHeight` uses this value)"; `:952-953` explicit AOSP FontMetrics law |
| N4 (ellipsize / maxLines) | `[F]` wrong — `:1386-1389` AOSP singleLine/maxLines=1 law; `:1435` "AOSP StaticLayout law `lines.size() <= maxLines`"; `:1448-1484` `TextUtils.ellipsize` START/MIDDLE/END |
| N6 (no bidi/shaping at all) | `[F]` wrong — FriBidi `:17`, HarfBuzz `:15-16`, `fribidi_log2vis` `:620`, `hb_shape` `:641` |
| N7 (no shaping for complex scripts) | partially wrong — HarfBuzz handles joining **if fed correctly**; see NEW-21 |

---

### NEW-21 (P0, `[V]`) — The entire **visually reordered** string is shaped as ONE run

`fonts/text_shaper.cpp:605-641`:
```cpp
std::u32string u32 = utf8_to_u32(utf8);
std::vector<FriBidiChar> src(u32.begin(), u32.end());
// FriBidi: first-strong base direction.
FriBidiParType base = FRIBIDI_PAR_LTR;
for (FriBidiChar ch : src) { … base = FRIBIDI_PAR_RTL … }
// Visual reorder (handles embedded opposite-direction segments).
std::vector<FriBidiChar> vis(src.size() + 1);
FriBidiLevel lvl = fribidi_log2vis(src.data(), (FriBidiStrIndex)src.size(),
                                   &base, vis.data(), nullptr, nullptr, nullptr);
…
// HarfBuzz shaping of the VISUAL sequence.
hb_buffer_t* buf = hb_buffer_create();
hb_buffer_add_utf32(buf, vis.data(), (int)src.size(), 0, -1);
hb_buffer_guess_segment_properties(buf);
hb_shape(hb_font, buf, nullptr, 0);
```

**Why this is wrong.** The correct architecture is: segment the logical string into runs that share script + direction + font, shape **each run in logical order**, then reorder the *shaped runs* visually. Here the characters are reordered first and the whole visual sequence is handed to `hb_shape` as a single run with **guessed** properties.

Consequences for Persian/Arabic:
1. **Joining forms are computed from reversed neighbours.** Arabic contextual shaping (`init`/`medi`/`fina`/`isol`) depends on the *logical* adjacency of letters. After `log2vis` the RTL run is reversed, so the shaper sees each letter's neighbours in the wrong order and selects wrong presentation forms → **disconnected or wrongly-joined letters**.
2. **`hb_buffer_guess_segment_properties` picks one script/direction for the whole visual string.** Mixed Persian + Latin + digits cannot be represented by one property set. The HarfBuzz manual is explicit: *"HarfBuzz expects to shape a run of characters that all share the same properties."* [[94]]
3. **Combining marks / diacritics attach to the wrong base** after reordering (Unicode bidi rule L3 exists precisely to handle mark reordering, and it must interact with shaping, not precede it).
4. **Bidi mirroring** of parentheses/brackets is applied by FriBidi, then HarfBuzz may mirror again depending on guessed direction — the known class of double-mirroring bugs [[76]].
5. `fribidi_log2vis` is called with `nullptr` for the embedding-levels output, so **per-run levels are discarded** — the information needed to do run segmentation is thrown away. That is the root cause enabling this design.

**Note on the HarfBuzz FAQ.** The manual does say *"Before sending your string to HarfBuzz, you may need to apply the bidi algorithm to it"* [[77]] [[78]] [[85]] — that advice means *use bidi to determine run boundaries and directions*, **not** *feed one globally-reversed buffer*. The distinction is exactly what breaks here.

**Correct pipeline (what AOSP does):** Minikin uses HarfBuzz for shaping and ICU bidi for reordering, operating on runs [[91]]. Reference implementation order:
```
1. itemize logical string into runs (script, bidi level, font, style)
2. for each run: hb_buffer_add_utf32(logical slice)
                 hb_buffer_set_script / set_direction / set_language explicitly
                 hb_shape()
3. measure advances, line-break (Minikin LineBreaker / ICU)
4. reorder shaped runs by bidi level for display
```
**Fix sketch:** request the levels array from FriBidi (`fribidi_log2vis(..., &base, vis, levels, nullptr, nullptr)`), split `src` into maximal equal-level+script runs, shape each logical slice with explicit `hb_buffer_set_direction(dir_from_level)` and `hb_buffer_set_script`, then place runs in visual order using `vis`/levels.

**Regression test (cheap and decisive):** shape the Persian string `سلام دنیا` and the mixed string `سلام Android 1405` and assert (a) every Arabic letter receives a non-isolated presentation form where context requires it, (b) total advance equals the sum of per-run advances, (c) the rendered glyph order matches a reference produced by Pango or by Android `StaticLayout`. A golden PNG per string.

### NEW-22 (P0/P1, `[V]`) — No font **fallback chain**: bold and fallback both alias to the regular face

`fonts/text_shaper.cpp:79-91`:
```cpp
if (!load_face_first(kFaceRegular)) available_ = false;
if (!load_face_first(kFaceBold)) {
    faces_[kFaceBold].ft_face = faces_[kFaceRegular].ft_face;
    … faces_[kFaceBold].aliased = true;
}
if (!load_face_first(kFaceFallback)) {
    faces_[kFaceFallback].ft_face = faces_[kFaceRegular].ft_face;
    … faces_[kFaceFallback].aliased = true;
}
```
The `aliased` flag is honest and good practice (`:74-78` explains it was added so a shaping bug cannot hide behind a silent substitution). **But there are only three slots: regular, bold, fallback.** AOSP `fonts.xml` defines an *ordered fallback list* — Noto Naskh Arabic, Noto Sans CJK, Noto Color Emoji, etc.

Consequences:
- If the regular face lacks Arabic glyphs and the fallback face is missing (→ aliased to regular), **every Persian codepoint renders `.notdef` tofu**.
- **Bold text is not bold** when the bold face is absent — silently regular weight.
- Emoji, CJK, Devanagari, Thai have no path at all.
- `:92-97` shows monospace is resolved from `runtime/data/fonts/` with a SHA-256-pinned NOTICE — so the font-shipping mechanism exists; it just needs more faces and a chain.

**Fix:** replace the 3-slot array with an ordered `std::vector<Face>` fallback chain, resolve per-codepoint via `FT_Get_Char_Index` (or HarfBuzz `hb_font_get_nominal_glyph`), and port the `fonts.xml` family/fallback ordering. Report `ALIASED`/`MISSING_GLYPH` per codepoint in the trace so tofu is never silent.
`[R]` AOSP `frameworks/base/data/fonts/fonts.xml` (the authoritative family + fallback order) https://android.googlesource.com/platform/frameworks/base/+/refs/heads/main/data/fonts/fonts.xml · `FontListParser` / `SystemFonts` in `frameworks/base/graphics/java/android/graphics/fonts/` · Noto fonts https://fonts.google.com/noto · FreeType `FT_Get_Char_Index` https://freetype.org/freetype2/docs/reference/ft2-base_interface.html#ft_get_char_index

### NEW-23 (P1, `[V]`) — Paragraph direction is first-strong only; no locale / `textDirection` heuristic
`:609-615` derives the base direction purely from the first strong character. AOSP `TextView` uses `TextDirectionHeuristic` (`FIRSTSTRONG_LTR`, `FIRSTSTRONG_RTL`, `LOCALE`, `ANYRTL_LTR`, …) with the **locale** as a fallback when no strong character exists. A string of digits/punctuation in a Persian locale should be RTL; here it stays LTR.
`[R]` https://developer.android.com/reference/android/text/TextDirectionHeuristics · `View.setTextDirection` https://developer.android.com/reference/android/view/View#setTextDirection(int)

### NEW-24 (P1, `[V]`) — Heuristic font metrics fallback
`:583-584`:
```cpp
if (result.ascent  <= 0) result.ascent  = size_px * 0.9f;
if (result.descent <= 0) result.descent = size_px * 0.25f;
```
Magic ratios substituted for real metrics. If a face reports zero metrics the line box silently becomes an approximation, which then disagrees with the AOSP `descent - ascent` law used elsewhere (`:840`). Should be a loud diagnostic + a documented fallback, not a silent guess.

### NEW-25 (P2, `[V]`) — Historical crash and API-drift notes worth pinning in CI
`:573` "the zero-scale `hb_font` crashed `hb_shape` (accelerace SIGSEGV)"; `:603` "`hb_ft_font_set_scale` call (API removed in newer HarfBuzz)". Both are guards against real upstream API drift. **Pin HarfBuzz/FreeType/FriBidi versions** in the build and add a smoke test that shapes at size 0 and at a fractional size, so an upstream bump cannot reintroduce the SIGSEGV.
`[R]` HarfBuzz API changelog https://github.com/harfbuzz/harfbuzz/blob/main/NEWS · `hb_ft_font_set_scale` removal note https://github.com/harfbuzz/harfbuzz/issues/2551

### NEW-26 (P2, `[V]`) — Residual over-allocation from the phantom-NUL fix
`:619` `std::vector<FriBidiChar> vis(src.size() + 1);` while `:636` correctly shapes `src.size()`. The MG-085 fix (`:628-634`) removed a real bug (a phantom U+0000 cluster inflating **every** TextView width). ## BATCH 6 — Resource system audit: faithful AOSP port, plus one **arbitrary style-value heuristic** that is a strong candidate for the "wrong colors" symptom

### L4 / L5 → `[F]` FALSIFIED. Reference resolution and config selection are real ports.

`resources/arsc_parser.cpp` (manifest TU, 1,223 lines):
```cpp
// :754-759
// GOLDEN-03 §4/§6 — canonical structured resolution.
// AOSP law: AssetManager2/ResTable resolveReference walks REFERENCE values
// entry-by-entry, each lookup selecting under the requested configuration.
// MiniAndroid adds the §6 safety contract: bounded depth + cycle detection +
// named deterministic errors (hostile tables must never loop or corrupt).
// :761-772  named errors: INVALID_ID / MISSING_ENTRY / MISSING_REFERENCE_TARGET
//                        / CYCLE / DEPTH_EXCEEDED / NOT_RESOLVABLE
// :820-826  correct terminal case — a bag is NOT a reference
if (e->is_complex) break;
if (!e->value.is_reference()) break;
next_id = e->value.ref_id;
// :868-870  attribute-key style-bag query WITH parent inheritance
```

`resources/res_config.cpp` (manifest TU, 456 lines) ports the AOSP qualifier precedence explicitly:
```cpp
// :4-8
```

### NEW-27 (P0 candidate, `[V]`) — A style bag's scalar value is set to its **first attribute**, arbitrarily

`resources/arsc_parser.cpp:361-362`:
```cpp
// style: first item often text color; keep simple value = first
if (!entry.complex_items.empty()) entry.value = entry.complex_items[0];
```

**Why this is a defect.** In AOSP a style entry is a **bag** (`ResTable_map` array of `{attr_id → Res_value}`) and has **no scalar value**. Assigning `complex_items[0]` to `entry.value` invents a scalar that does not exist, and which attribute lands first is an **aapt2 ordering artifact**, not semantics.

**Predicted symptom chain:** any consumer that reads `entry.value` without first checking `is_complex` will receive the first style attribute's value. Because the first item is *often* `textColor` (as the comment itself admits), a lookup intended to produce a **background** or a **dimension** can silently return a **color**, and a color lookup can return the wrong color. That is precisely the reported *"Colors are missing, swapped, flattened, or painted into incorrect regions."*

Note the resolution path itself is careful (`:824 if (e->is_complex) break;`), so the exposure is in **other** consumers of `entry.value`. This is a grep-and-audit task, not a rewrite.

**Probe (decisive, ~30 min):**
1. Find every read of `entry.value` / `ResEntry::value` across `arsc_parser.cpp`, `resource_runtime.cpp`, `layout_inflater.cpp`, `theme_engine.h`.

3. Build a test APK with a style whose first attribute is `textColor` and whose second is `background`, request `background` through the style, and confirm the returned value is the background color and not the text color.

**Fix:** remove the assignment; make `value` unset for bags and force callers through the attribute-keyed bag query (`:868-870` already implements it with parent inheritance). ## BATCH 7 — NEW-14 **CONFIRMED**: CENTER / CENTER_CROP images are drawn with **no clip**, so they paint outside their ImageView

This is now a verified live rendering defect with an exact file:line, and it directly matches the reported symptom *"Images are incorrectly scaled, cropped, or positioned."*

### The call site
`runtime/execution_engine.cpp:5299-5309` (manifest TU):
```cpp
int pl = node->padding_left, pt = node->padding_top;
int pr = node->padding_right, pb = node->padding_bottom;
renderer::FitRect fr = g04_image_draw_rect(
    decoded.width, decoded.height, sel_d,
    left + pl, top + pt,
    std::max(1, w - pl - pr),
    std::max(1, h - pt - pb),
    node->scale_type);
canvas.draw_image(decoded.rgba.data(),
                  decoded.width, decoded.height,
                  fr.x, fr.y, fr.w, fr.h);
```
**There is no `canvas.set_clip(...)` between computing `fr` and drawing.** The clip primitive exists — `SoftwareCanvas::set_clip(left, top, right, bottom)` at `renderer/software_renderer.cpp:158`, documented as the AOSP `clipRect` law (`:157`) — it is simply not used here.

### Why it overflows
`renderer/software_renderer.cpp:440-453`:
```cpp
case 5:  // CENTER — natural size, centered
    r.w = src_w; r.h = src_h;
    r.x = box_x + (box_w - src_w) / 2;      // NEGATIVE offset when src_w > box_w
    r.y = box_y + (box_h - src_h) / 2;
case 6: { // CENTER_CROP — crop-scale, centered
    const float crop = std::max(float(box_w)/src_w, float(box_h)/src_h);
    r.w = lround(src_w * crop);             // ALWAYS >= box_w
    r.h = lround(src_h * crop);             // ALWAYS >= box_h
    r.x = box_x + (box_w - r.w) / 2;        // NEGATIVE offset
    r.y = box_y + (box_h - r.h) / 2;
}
```
`CENTER_CROP` **by definition** produces a rect larger than the view on one axis; AOSP achieves the crop by clipping the drawable to the view bounds. Without the clip, MiniAndroid draws the **whole scaled bitmap**, overflowing onto siblings and parent padding. `CENTER` overflows whenever the asset is larger than the view. `MATRIX` (`:421-424`, natural size at box origin) overflows the same way.

**Affected scaleTypes:** 0 MATRIX, 5 CENTER, 6 CENTER_CROP. FIT_* and CENTER_INSIDE are safe because their rects are ≤ the box by construction.

### Fix (3 lines, plus the same guard at the other two call sites)
```cpp
canvas.set_clip(left + pl, top + pt,
                left + pl + std::max(1, w - pl - pr),
                top + pt  + std::max(1, h - pt - pb));
renderer::FitRect fr = g04_image_draw_rect(...);
canvas.draw_image(...);
// restore the previous clip afterwards (save/restore discipline)
```
The same pattern must be applied at the other two `node->scale_type` call sites: **`execution_engine.cpp:5513` and `:5570`**. All three go through `g04_image_draw_rect` (`:73-100`), so an alternative is to push the clip inside that helper — but it returns a rect rather than drawing, so the clip belongs at each draw site.

- `CENTER`: same assertion.
- `FIT_CENTER`: assert the letterbox margins show the view background, not the asset.
Tolerance 1 px. Golden PNGs per scaleType.

```cpp
//     the app override onCreate(SQLiteDatabase) (virtual, real DEX) and
```

## §B. Eight new verified defects (all `[V]`, file:line)

### SQL-1 (P0) — `beginTransaction` and `beginTransactionNonExclusive` both emit plain `BEGIN;`
`sqlite_shadow.cpp:473-476`:
```cpp
if (m == "beginTransaction" || m == "beginTransactionNonExclusive") {
    …
    sqlite3_exec(raw, "BEGIN;", nullptr, nullptr, &err);
```
**Upstream law:** `SQLiteDatabase.beginTransaction()` acquires an **EXCLUSIVE** lock; `beginTransactionNonExclusive()` acquires an **IMMEDIATE** lock (allowing other readers). Plain `BEGIN` is **DEFERRED** — it takes no lock until the first read/write.
**Consequence:** lock acquisition timing differs, `SQLITE_BUSY` surfaces at a different statement, and the two APIs are indistinguishable. Any app relying on `beginTransactionNonExclusive` for reader concurrency gets exclusive-ish behaviour at the wrong moment.
**Fix:** `BEGIN EXCLUSIVE;` vs `BEGIN IMMEDIATE;`.
`[R]` `SQLiteDatabase.beginTransaction()` / `beginTransactionNonExclusive()` contracts: https://developer.android.com/reference/android/database/sqlite/SQLiteDatabase#beginTransaction() and https://developer.android.com/reference/android/database/sqlite/SQLiteDatabase#beginTransactionNonExclusive() · AOSP source https://android.googlesource.com/platform/frameworks/base/+/master/core/java/android/database/sqlite/SQLiteDatabase.java [[4]] · SQLite locking semantics https://www.sqlite.org/lang_transaction.html

### SQL-2 (P0) — `onConfigure` and `onDowngrade` are never called; `needUpgrade` absent
`grep -E 'onConfigure|onDowngrade|needUpgrade'` over 1,442 lines → **0 hits**.
**Upstream law:** `SQLiteOpenHelper.getDatabaseLocked()` calls, in order: `onConfigure(db)` → version check → `onCreate` / `onUpgrade` / `onDowngrade` → `onOpen(db)`. `onDowngrade`'s default implementation **throws** `SQLiteException("Can't downgrade database from version X to Y")`.
**Consequence:** (a) an app that configures the DB in `onConfigure` (Room, SQLCipher, `setForeignKeyConstraintsEnabled`, WAL setup) never gets it; (b) a version **downgrade silently succeeds** where Android would throw — silent data-schema corruption instead of a loud failure.
**Fix:** add `pending_configure` and `pending_downgrade` flags alongside the existing `pending_create`/`pending_upgrade`/`pending_open`, consumed engine-side by the same `try_recursive_invoke` protocol; default `onDowngrade` must throw.
`[R]` AOSP `SQLiteOpenHelper.java` — read `getDatabaseLocked` end to end: https://android.googlesource.com/platform/frameworks/base/+/HEAD/core/java/android/database/sqlite/SQLiteOpenHelper.java [[2]] (stable tag copy: https://android.googlesource.com/platform/frameworks/base/+/android-8.0.0_r36/core/java/android/database/sqlite/SQLiteOpenHelper.java [[1]]) · API docs https://developer.android.com/reference/android/database/sqlite/SQLiteOpenHelper [[3]]

### SQL-3 (P0) — Full result-set materialization replaces `CursorWindow`; unbounded memory, wrong exception surface
`sqlite_shadow.h:143-157` `CursorState { std::vector<std::vector<Cell>> rows; }`; `sqlite_shadow.cpp:879` "Materialize the full result set (deterministic single-thread law)."
**Upstream law:** `SQLiteCursor` fills a **`CursorWindow`** (default **2 MB**) lazily, starting at a fixed initial count, and refills as the cursor moves. Android does **not** load all rows into memory at once [[24]]. The Android team's own writeup explains the fixed-initial-load design [[25]], and the 2 MB limit is confirmed in the field [[26]]; `CursorWindow` is the documented buffer abstraction [[27]].
**Consequences:**
1. A 100k-row query allocates the whole result set — on a memory-constrained host this is an OOM where Android would stream.
2. `CursorWindowAllocationException` ("Row too big to fit into CursorWindow") can never be produced, so apps that handle it are untested [[26]].
3. `CursorWindow`-dependent APIs (`getWindow()`, `setWindow()`, `CursorWindow.size()`) have no backing.
**Note:** determinism does **not** require full materialization. A deterministic single-threaded runtime can fill a bounded window lazily and still be byte-reproducible, because the step order is fixed. **The stated justification for the deviation does not hold.**
**Fix:** implement a bounded `CursorWindow` (2 MB default, `CursorWindow.size()`), lazy `fillWindow(startPos)` on `moveTo*`, and the allocation exception. Port the algorithm rather than invent it.
`[R]` AOSP `SQLiteConnection.java` (`executeForCursorWindow`, `CursorWindow window = new CursorWindow(...)`) https://android.googlesource.com/platform/frameworks/base/+/master/core/java/android/database/sqlite/SQLiteConnection.java [[29]] · **native law** `android_database_SQLiteConnection.cpp` (`nativeExecuteForCursorWindow`) — this is the C++ function to port, see §C.

`sqlite_shadow.cpp:1411-1412`: "getType (Cursor.FIELD_TYPE_*): NULL=0, INTEGER=1, FLOAT=2, TEXT=3, **BLOB=4 (no BLOB materialization yet — honest scope note)**"; `sqlite_shadow.h:148-153` `Cell::Kind { LONG, DOUBLE, STRING, NULLV }` — no BLOB.
**Consequence:** `getBlob()` cannot work; `getType()` cannot return 4. Room entities with `byte[]`/`ByteArray` columns (avatars, cached payloads, encrypted blobs) silently lose data. The header already records the identical class of bug being fixed for FLOAT (**F-NEW-401**: "SQLITE_FLOAT previously collapsed into int64 (2.5 materialized as 2 — silent data corruption)"). BLOB is the same bug, still open.
**Fix:** add `Kind::BLOB` + `std::vector<uint8_t> blob_val`, map `SQLITE_BLOB`, implement `getBlob`.

### SQL-5 (P1) — `CursorFactory` is accepted and ignored
`rawQueryWithFactory` / `queryWithFactory` are handled (`:1039`) but `grep newCursor|CursorFactory` finds only the constructor comment at `:342` — **`newCursor(...)` is never invoked**.
**Upstream law:** when a non-null `SQLiteDatabase.CursorFactory` is supplied, `SQLiteCursor` construction goes through `factory.newCursor(db, masterQuery, editTable, query)`. Apps subclass `SQLiteCursor` to add behaviour; that subclass never runs here.
**Fix:** engine-side `try_recursive_invoke` on the factory object, same protocol already used for `onCreate`/`onOpen`.
`[R]` https://developer.android.com/reference/android/database/sqlite/SQLiteDatabase.CursorFactory · `SQLiteCursor` constructors in AOSP `SQLiteCursor.java`.

### SQL-6 (P1) — WAL is set but the connection pool is not, so WAL buys nothing
`:232-241` and `:395-403` apply `PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL` / `DELETE` correctly and trace the `-wal`/`-shm` file family. But the law block fixes **one connection** (`sqlite_shadow.h:18-21`).

`grep busy_timeout` → 0 hits. With `SQLITE_BUSY` possible from an external process or a second connection, statements fail immediately instead of retrying. AOSP configures contention handling in `SQLiteConnection`/`SQLiteConnectionPool`.

`[R]` https://www.sqlite.org/c3ref/busy_timeout.html · AOSP `SQLiteConnectionPool.java` [[28]]

## Proposed constitution amendment (one paragraph, large compounding payoff)

> **§170 (amended) — SUBSYSTEM SOURCE-FIRST LAW.** The mandatory ordered hunt currently applies to graphics. Extend it to **every** subsystem family: resources/AXML/ARSC, storage/SQLite, input/physics, text/bidi, webview/HTML/CSS, animation, and concurrency. Each family gets a registry (`docs/<FAMILY>_SOURCE_REGISTRY.md` + `.json`) with the same fields (`reuse_class`, `license_class`, pinned SHA, upstream tests). Before writing more than ~50 LOC in any family: STOP, query the family registry and `cs.android.com`, record `SEARCHED → SOURCE FOUND/NOT FOUND → LICENSE CHECKED → REUSE DECISION`, then continue.

Rationale grounded in this audit: the graphics family got a 122-repository registry and produced a faithful engine (BATCH 4 confirmed the layout/graphics laws are correct ports). The families **without** a registry produced a 20-byte stride bug, a missing CursorWindow, missing nine-patch, three competing vector parsers, and a 343 KB hand-written webview. **The registry is the intervention that worked.** Generalize it.
